messages.author: 11021af02c59100d
messages.subject: MSstatsPTM::PDtoMSstatsPTMFormat issue
parts:
Hello. 
I have been using the MSstatsPTM to process the ptm datasets and recently updated to latest version 2.4.3. Thank you so much for developing this package, which allows us to process and normalize ptm dataset easily!

we have both whole proteome data and ptm enriched data from Proteome Discoverer. 

I used to be able to get 'PROTEIN' and 'PTM' dataframe from PDtoMSstatsPTMFormat, but the PDtoMSstatsPTMFormat only gives me the 'PTM' dataframe now, even we supply the whole proteome level data in the input 
 
The section below is how I called the function. 

ptm_input = MSstatsPTM::PDtoMSstatsPTMFormat(input = pd_ptm,
                                             annotation = ann_ptm,
                                             fasta_path = fastafile,
                                             protein_input = pd_proteome,
                                             annotation_protein = ann_proteome,
                                             use_log_file = T,
                                             mod_id = mod_tag,
                                             labeling_type='TMT',
                                             which_proteinid='Master.Protein.Accessions')

Both whole proteome and ptm data sets is provided, but the resulting ptm_input object only has 'PTM' information 

Here is what I got when using str(ptm_input)
> str(ptm_input)
List of 1
 $ PTM:'data.frame': 587682 obs. of  11 variables:
  ..$ ProteinName    :
  ..$ PeptideSequence: 
  ..$ Charge         : 
  ..$ PSM            : 
  ..$ Mixture        : 
  ..$ TechRepMixture : 
  ..$ Run            : 
  ..$ Channel        : 
  ..$ BioReplicate   : 
  ..$ Condition      : 
  ..$ Intensity      : 
  ..- attr(*, ".S3Class")= chr "data.frame"

To figure out what happed, I looked into the code in the MSstatsPTM gitlab codebase for release_3_17 and release_3_18. 

I found that the PDtoMSstatsPTMFormat function in converts.R in release_3_18 has a couple of more lines in the bottom.

if (use_unmod_peptides){
    ptm_input=as.data.frame(ptm_input)
    protein_input = ptm_input[!grepl(mod_id, ptm_input$PeptideSequence),]
    ptm_input = ptm_input[grepl(mod_id, ptm_input$PeptideSequence),]
   
    msstats_input = list(PTM = ptm_input, PROTEIN = protein_input)
  } else {
    ptm_input = ptm_input[grepl("\\*", ptm_input[, "PeptideSequence"]), ]
   
    msstats_input = list(PTM = ptm_input)  <- this is why PROTEIN result is missing when use_unmod_peptides is FALSE which is default value
  }
 
Should I add the PROTEIN result back manually with PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat, or this was done on purpose, and we are not supposed to have the protein level data when the use_unmod_peptides is FALSE ?

Can you give us some advices? 

Thank you
Best, 

Han-Yin

Apologies this was a mistake and has now been fixed. You can download the updated version from Github now (version 2.5.4), or download the bug fix directly from Bioconductor tomorrow (version 2.4.4).

Devon
